title: Happiness and Time Preference: The Effect of Positive Affect in a Random-Assignment Experiment

original_source.version_note: Complete original abstract only; full body inaccessible through attempted publisher/author routes.

central_claims: Mild positive affect reduces time preference over money relative to neutral affect in a randomized experiment.

source_manifest.title: Happiness and Time Preference: The Effect of Positive Affect in a Random-Assignment Experiment
source_manifest.finding: Original central claims were recorded before follow-up grading.

source_manifest.title: Camerer et al. Evaluating replicability of laboratory experiments in economics — Supplement, Tables S1–S2
source_manifest.finding: The preregistered independent comparison tests whether a positive-affect film raises patience among participants who discount; replication N=131, original focal N=58, p=.933. The project only retested one selected result per paper.

source_manifest.title: Diagnosing the role of observable distribution shift in scientific replications
source_manifest.finding: Independent reanalysis finds observed mood/covariate shifts do not explain the emotion–patience discrepancy; unobserved differences or selection/publication bias remain possible.

answers.rationale: No unambiguous later independent support for the stated central claim was established in the sources read.
The available evidence does not settle successful independent reproduction of the central claim.

The film-treatment patience result did not survive the larger independent replication. Subsequent reweighting for observed mood induction and demographics also did not restore the effect. This does not establish that all positive emotion has no causal influence on patience.

research.summary: The film-treatment patience result failed independent replication. Later data reanalysis could not explain the discrepancy using measured mood and demographic shifts; the original data remain useful for methodological diagnosis. The general causal claim remains uncertain.
